key_insight: A dual-tier framework combines telemetry-based sentiment regression detection with multimodal layout diagnostics to identify web-search UX problems at scale.
engineering_relevance: The architecture supports faster A/B-test evaluation and targeted UX debugging while reducing reliance on surveys.
method: Macro tier: fine-tune a Gemini XS–based encoder-decoder model on telemetry using multi-task regularization and contextual features.
Micro tier: use Gemini 3.0 Pro to assess rendered results and spatial layout, estimating effort as “User Toil.”
Refine micro-tier diagnostics with RL-based prompt optimization and an AI judge for win/loss patterns.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports +9.8% PR-AUC on over 500,000 held-out records, approximately 20% relative precision gain at matched baseline recall across 12 held-out experiments, and >6.5% F1 improvement for the multimodal tier.
watch_item: Validate model-derived sentiment and User Toil against human judgments across changing search layouts; the abstract does not establish generalization beyond the reported setting.
paper_title: The Dual-Tier Sentiment Framework: Scalable Multimodal UX Attribution in Web Search
